Point `(120,120)` lies inside all three absolutely-positioned boxes’ `getBoundingClientRect()` areas:  
- `root>back`: `(40..240, 40..240)`  
- `root>middle`: `(80..280, 80..280)`  
- `root>front`: `(100..160, 100..160)`  

When multiple positioned elements overlap, the one with the highest `z-index` is painted on top. Their computed `z-index` values are: back `1`, front `2`, middle `3`, so `root>middle` is what a viewer sees at that point.

ANSWER: root>middle
